prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map separates the near brick path and nearby people from the mid-distance lawn, wall, gate, and trees; approximate distances are non-metric, but the closest partial people at the right edges of frames 1, 4, and 5 appear about 0.5–1.5 m away, while the fully visible person in frames 4–5 is roughly 2–4 m ahead. The gate-side potted plants are about 2–5 m away and the cars beyond the gate roughly 8–15 m away; the people in frames 4–5 are approximately 2–3 m apart, with the partial person to the camera’s right and slightly closer. Across the strip, the view turns from the gate toward the path; the full person remains ahead and faces mostly away or toward the left side of the path, while the right-edge person stays very close and partly outside the view, with no clear evidence that either looks at the camera. Bright silhouettes and the ground gradient make relative proximity and occlusion clearer than RGB alone, but absolute metre estimates, thin limbs, object boundaries, and distant dark regions are unreliable, and brightness changes may reflect prediction artifacts rather than true distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map explicitly locates two potted plants and cars around the left-side gate in the first three frames, then people in the later view along the path; the plants are roughly 2–5 m from the camera and separated by several metres, while the cars are farther behind them at about 8–15 m. A partial person lies at the right edge of frame 1, a full person stands or moves about 2–4 m ahead in frames 4–5, and another person is only partly visible at the right edge about 0.5–1.5 m away; the nearer person is plausibly within the camera wearer’s arm reach, whereas the full person is not. The full person is ahead and slightly left of the nearer right-edge person, with the two roughly 2–3 m apart; their masks show occlusion by the image boundary but do not reliably reveal gaze or front-versus-back orientation. The masks make object identity and instance boundaries clearer than RGB, especially for small cars and cropped people, but most of the path, wall, vegetation, carried items, and scene structure remain black, and some detections appear to disappear between frames despite still-visible scene content.
descriptions.pose: The pose map detects one full-body skeleton in frames 4 and 5, placing that person roughly 2–4 m in front of the camera and beyond arm’s reach; the upright torso, separated legs, and asymmetric arms show body configuration more clearly than RGB. In frame 4 the body is angled mostly side-on while facing generally away and toward the left side of the path, and by frame 5 it appears more turned away/down the path; the head markers do not establish that the person looks toward the camera. The skeleton shifts from near the centre-right of frame 4 to near the centre of frame 5 as the camera view turns, while the very close person at the right edge—about 0.5–1.5 m away and partly out of view—receives no pose, so spacing and mutual reach cannot be fully assessed from this map. Pose is unreliable for precise depth, gaze, hands, and occlusion: no magenta hand skeletons are visible, several joints near the head and arms are ambiguous, and people visible or cropped in other frames are missed entirely.
